subject: Hosted API pricing: usage profile, burst needs, and budget sensitivity
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Lily Chen <lily@finpay.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@finpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing: usage profile, burst needs, and budget sensitivity

Hi Lily / Devon —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clear context on where FinPay wants to use LLMs (transaction tagging + customer support assist). Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the usage shape we discussed and a few specific asks so we can produce a clean hosted pricing quote: 

Summary of what I heard (please correct):
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~95M–140M tokens (metric: input + output tokens combined).
- Typical daily profile: steady baseline during business hours with 1–2 short flash windows per week.
- Peak TPS (concurrent token throughput): you called out ~12 TPS typically, but possible flash bursts up to ~18 TPS during promo windows.
- Latency target: p95 <= 400ms for single-shot generation; p50 much lower.
- Procurement preference: prefer pay-as-you-go but open to 6–12 month commit if economics materially improve.

Questions / asks for the quote:
1) Can you confirm a likely committed monthly token target (e.g., pick a number in the middle – 120M?)
2) Are the flash bursts short (minutes) or sustained (tens of minutes)? That affects whether we recommend reserved burst capacity vs transient autoscaling.
3) Target budget range for hosted inference (monthly)? You mentioned ballpark ranges on the call but I want a concrete range we can use to compute $/1M tokens.

I attached a lightweight usage_workbook_v3.xlsx where we can both drop month-by-month token estimates. If you can fill the yellow cells I’ll run through cost bands and send a formal quote with a committed-rate comparison. Also attaching a draft_SLA_finpay_2027-08.pdf that shows our hosted availability/latency guarantees and burst policy.

Next steps: if you can reply with confirmed monthly target + how long bursts last, I’ll have Ben (copied) produce pricing bands and an indicative $/1M tokens for both pay-as-you-go and a 6- or 12-month commit.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Lily Chen <lily@finpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Park <devon.park@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: usage profile, burst needs, and budget sensitivity

Thanks Karthik — quick clarifications below.

Confirmed items:
- Monthly tokens: our best estimate right now is 110M–130M tokens/month (we're comfortable using 120M as the working number for a quote).
- Burst behavior: typical flashes are 5–12 minutes (usually under 10 minutes), but we run a quarterly promo that can push traffic for ~30 minutes at higher rates. During those promos we could hit ~18 TPS for short periods.
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms is our goal — important for user experience in the support use case.

Budget: Internal stakeholders have penciled ~USD 7k–12k/month for hosted inference for Year 1. That’s flexible if the unit economics make sense, but we’d like to understand effective $/1M tokens at 120M/mo and how that changes with a 6–12 month commit (and whether burst protection increases cost materially).

One more ask: can you show both (a) pay-as-you-go per-1M token pricing and (b) an effective $/1M for a 6-month and 12-month committed band? Also call out whether peak TPS/short bursts trigger any additional fees or require a separate reserved burst pool.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up call after you send the bands.

Thanks,
Lily Chen
Head of Product Ops | FinPay Inc.
lily@finpay.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Lily Chen <lily@finpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Devon Park <devon.park@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: usage profile, burst needs, and budget sensitivity

Hi Lily — looping in a quick pricing sketch so you have numbers to work with. Below are ballpark bands (indicative; we’ll produce a formal quote once you confirm the 120M baseline and preferred term).

High-level pricing (hosted API, model family equivalent to our medium-latency offering):
- Pay-as-you-go: ~$85 per 1M tokens (no commit; includes standard autoscaling and 30s cold-starts for new instances).
- 6-month commit (120M/mo avg): effective ~$63 per 1M tokens (volume discount applied; commitment offsets capacity planning).
- 12-month commit (120M/mo avg): effective ~$52 per 1M tokens (largest discount; best unit economics).

Notes on burst TPS and fees:
- Short bursts (<= 10 minutes) are handled by our autoscaler and are included in hosted pricing up to a configurable burst factor (we typically allow 1.5x baseline TPS without extra charge).
- Sustained bursts beyond the configured window (e.g., repeated 30+ minute high TPS events) are best covered by a small reserved burst pool — that is charged as a reserved capacity premium (one-time setup + modest monthly commit). For FinPay's described pattern, we expect the autoscaler to handle most events; the quarterly 30-minute promo may be a candidate for a modest reserved burst pool.
- Caching and batching (recommended for support flows) can reduce effective token count by ~10–25% depending on prompt overlap; we can model that in the workbook.

Example math at 120M tokens/mo: 
- PAYG: 120 * $85 = $10,200 / month.
- 6-month: 120 * $63 = $7,560 / month.
- 12-month: 120 * $52 = $6,240 / month.

I attached pricing_bands_estimate.csv with the three bands and sensitivity rows for 95M and 140M monthly volume. If you want an alternate model (e.g., different model family or stronger latency SLO) Ben and I can re-run.

Action items:
- If 120M is confirmed and you prefer a 6 or 12 month term I’ll draft a formal quote and include a modest reserved burst recommendation for the quarterly promo.
- If you'd like to optimize unit economics we can also scope a small POC to measure real-world token counts and caching impact.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: usage profile, burst needs, and budget sensitivity

Lily — thanks for the fast turnaround and helpful detail. Quick summary + next steps: 

Summary:
- Working baseline: 120M tokens / month; expect short bursts and one quarterly 30-minute promo that could reach ~18 TPS.
- Budget window: $7k–12k / month (target for Year 1).
- Indicative economics from Ben: PAYG ~$85/1M, 6-month ~$63/1M, 12-month ~$52/1M (see attached CSV for sensitivity).

Next steps I’ll take: 
1) Prepare a formal quote with 6- and 12-month committed options and a recommended reserved burst pool for promo windows. I’ll include line items for the reserved burst premium so you can see the tradeoff.
2) Share a DocuSign link for an optional 30-day POC/credits agreement if you want to test before committing.
3) Schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review the quote and finalize procurement cadence — are you available Tues 10–11am PT or Wed 2–3pm PT?

If that all looks good I’ll produce the quote by Monday EOD.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
—Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
